title: Deleting a message deletes nothing: an outsider learns what was deleted, a member reads the text back, and an unauthenticated caller reads it too

steps.action: call chat.getDeletedMessages for a private group's id as an account that is not a member of it
steps.result: the ids and timestamps of that room's deletions, from a caller that cannot open the room at all (groups.history answers HTTP 400 for the same account)

steps.action: as a member, call chat.syncThreadsList for the room with an updatedSince earlier than the deletion
steps.result: the full text of a deleted thread root on the shipped configuration, with Message_KeepHistory still false, while the room's own history withholds it

steps.action: with Message_KeepHistory on, call chat.getMessage with a deleted message's id
steps.result: the text of an ordinary deleted message, not just a thread root, returned to a member while the room's history does not show it

steps.action: with Accounts_AllowAnonymousRead on, request channels.anonymousread for the same channel with no credentials of any kind
steps.result: the same deleted message and the deleted thread root returned to an unauthenticated caller

combined_impact: Proven in the lab: a message a user deleted on purpose was recoverable at three different distances from the room. An account with no relationship to a private group listed its deletions with their ids and times; a member recovered a deleted thread root's full text on the configuration Rocket.Chat ships; with history keeping on a member recovered an ordinary deleted message's text by id; and with anonymous read on, an unauthenticated request returned both texts. Attacker capability before: see a message removed stub, like everyone else. After: the deletion timeline of rooms it cannot see, the content of deleted messages in rooms it can, and, where anonymous read is on, that content with no account at all. The blast radius is everything anybody deleted because it should not have been said: pasted credentials (the run planted one), customer details, a sentence about a colleague. The run also recorded the interaction that bounds this: with history keeping on nothing is moved to the trash collection, so the timeline leak and the content leak apply in opposite configurations, and each is enough on its own for the step that follows it.
preconditions: Any authenticated account for step 1, which needs only the room id (ids travel in permalinks, invites and several API responses). Membership of the room for steps 2 and 3. Nothing at all for step 4. Steps 3 and 4 need the business features Message_KeepHistory and Accounts_AllowAnonymousRead, both off by default, which the run turns on through the workspace's own settings API and restores; step 2 needs neither.
fix_order: Fix the one shared defect behind steps 2, 3 and 4: filter hidden documents in the readers that do not, namely chat.getMessage (getSingleMessage.ts:7-19), chat.syncThreadsList (chat.ts:1212), channels.anonymousread (channels.ts:2116-2122) and the personal-data export (exportRoomMessagesToFile.ts:217-218), the same _hidden filter the list, search and history routes already apply. One change, in four callers of the same pattern, removes the content disclosure at every distance, leaving only the deletion metadata. Side effect: keeps the feature and removes only the weakness: moderators keep reading message history through the feature built for it, and clients that catch up through the sync route stop receiving deleted documents (they learn of the deletion from the deletion list instead, which is what the route is for). The missing authorization on chat.getDeletedMessages (VULN-010) still needs its own room access check, since the timeline alone tells an outsider when a room is active and what was retracted.
